title: Implementation of a Sports Counseling Center for People with Congenital Heart Defects and Its Impact on Health-Related Quality of Life: A Pre- and Post-Intervention Study Involving Affected Children, Adolescents, and Adults.
summary:
People with congenital heart defects are sometimes unsure about how much exercise they can safely do. The goal of the study is to determine whether a personalized exercise program is safe and has positive effects on fitness and quality of life.
An initial and final test on a treadmill is used to assess individual fitness levels. In addition, participants are asked about their health-related quality of life. Based on the results of the exercise testing, a personalized endurance training plan is created at the start of the program, which the participant then carries out independently at home. After 6 months, a follow-up test is conducted, and the questionnaires are completed again.

interventions.name: A single-arm intervention over a 6-month period involving the implementation of an individualized training plan based on the CPET results from the initial assessment. The training plan is carried out independently over 12 weeks at a rate of 2–3 sessions per week and is gradually increased. Children

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Known congenital heart disease
Ability to undergo CPET
Sufficient knowledge of German (at least B2 level)
Consent
Exclusion criteria:
Acute cardiac decompensation
High-risk patients, e.g., those who have recently (≤3 months) undergone cardiac surgery, have an implanted defibrillator with progressive arrhythmias, or have severe pulmonary hypertension
(New) diagnosis of severe, additional (chronic) conditions that contraindicate exercise
Cognitive or mental impairments that make adequate informed consent or active participation impossible
Lack of informed consent
